Describe a segmentation configuration

Source: R/doc-segment-run.R
gr_segment_spec.Rd

Describe a segmentation configuration

Usage

gr_segment_spec(
  method = "paragraph",
  max_tokens = 1200L,
  overlap_tokens = 0L,
  min_tokens = 0L,
  separators = NULL,
  prefix_section = TRUE,
  semantic_window = 2L,
  semantic_percentile = 90,
  context_source = c("metadata", "llm"),
  proposition_batch_tokens = 900L,
  parallel = NULL,
  context_reply_tokens = 90L,
  context_document_tokens = 1500L,
  proposition_reply_tokens = 2000L,
  semantic_threshold = c("percentile", "texttiling"),
  table_packing = c("rows", "grouped"),
  proposition_check = c("count", "drop"),
  proposition_context_tokens = 0L,
  packing = c("greedy", "balanced"),
  runt_merge = c("backward", "both"),
  ...
)

Arguments

method

Segmenter name; see gr_segmenters().

max_tokens

Hard cap on chunk size, in tokens. Always enforced: a segmenter cannot emit an oversized chunk, which the old chunk_text_semantic() routinely did. An oversized chunk is re-split, down to single characters if it has to be; if the active tokenizer counts even one character as more than the cap, gr_segment() stops with an error of class "gr_cap_unenforceable" rather than pass the chunk on.

overlap_tokens

Tokens of trailing context copied into the start of the next chunk. Overlap is what stops an answer straddling a boundary from being lost by both chunks. Honoured by every segmenter except page (a page is the unit) and proposition (propositions are already self-contained). It is cut at sentences, then words; text written without spaces (Chinese, Japanese, Thai) is cut by characters. A chunk's page, section and block count the overlap it opens with, so one that carries a sentence from the page before reports NA rather than the page it goes on to.

min_tokens

A chunk smaller than this is merged backward into the chunk before it (and, with runt_merge = "both", a first chunk smaller than this forward into the one after it). Ignored by page and fixed.

separators

For method = "recursive": the cascade, strongest first. Each piece keeps the separator it was cut at; past the last one, text is cut at sentence ends, then whitespace, then characters, the same way. With no overlap, the chunks joined end to end are the document text exactly.

prefix_section

For method = "structural": prepend the heading. When the extractor supplies no sections, headings are found inline: a markdown # line, or a short line that is numbered and starts with a capital of any script (or a letter of a script without case), or is in capitals.

semantic_window, semantic_percentile

For method = "semantic": how many sentences to embed together, and how extreme a distance counts as a boundary (higher = fewer, larger chunks).

context_source

For method = "contextual": "metadata" (free) or "llm" (one call per chunk, never more: $extra$cost declares calls_max as the number of chunks, and a segment.cost trace step records it). Under "llm" each request carries the opening of the document (context_document_tokens) and the chunk's section path, as "Methods > Participants", from the document's headings. Room for the context line is held back from each chunk's text before packing (context_reply_tokens for "llm", the longest header the document could need for "metadata", never more than half of max_tokens), so no chunk is cut again once its header is added, and a header that still does not fit is shortened, never the text. Under "llm", a chunk whose call failed or was skipped at the run's limits keeps its text without a context line; $extra$blurbs_missing counts them and a "gr_segment_fallback" warning says so, which also reaches the answer's warnings.

proposition_batch_tokens

For method = "proposition": batch size. A proposition with no support in its batch (a number the batch does not give, or fewer than half of its words found in the batch and any context it was sent with) is counted in $extra$propositions_unsupported; see proposition_check. The chunks keep the page and section of the batches they come from.

parallel

Parallelise per-chunk model work in segmenters that do any.

context_reply_tokens

For method = "contextual" with context_source = "llm": the output cap of each context-line request, and the room held back for the line in each chunk. [16, 4000], default 90. Untested.

context_document_tokens

For context_source = "llm": how much of the document, from its start, each context-line request carries so the model can place the excerpt. [100, 1e6], default 1500. Untested.

proposition_reply_tokens

For method = "proposition": the output cap of each batch's request. [100, 1e6], default 2000. Untested.

semantic_threshold

For method = "semantic": how boundaries are chosen. "percentile" (the default) cuts wherever the distance between two consecutive windows reaches the semantic_percentile of all of them, so about one gap in ten is cut whatever the text is about. "texttiling" cuts by depth score, as TextTiling does (Hearst, M. A. 1997, "TextTiling: segmenting text into multi-paragraph subtopic passages", Computational Linguistics 23(1), 33-64): each gap's similarity is the cosine between the semantic_window sentences before it and the semantic_window after it (the same windows, so no extra embedding request), its depth is how far that similarity sits below the nearest peak on each side, summed, and a gap is cut when it is a valley whose depth exceeds Hearst's cutoff (the mean depth less half its standard deviation) and also exceeds the spread of the similarities (largest less smallest). That second test is added here, not Hearst's, so a text on one topic gets at most about one cut. semantic_percentile is not used under "texttiling". Untested.

table_packing

For method = "paragraph": how the rows of a table are packed. "rows" (the default) packs them as any other blocks, as before. "grouped" packs each table on its own: its first row, taken for the header, opens every chunk of the table, followed by as many rows as fit under max_tokens, joined by line breaks and with no overlap, so a 60-row table that needs three chunks gives three, each starting with the header. A table that fits is one chunk. Under either, the chunks of a document with a table carry table_id and table_rows (as "2-21") saying which table and rows they hold. Untested.

proposition_check

For method = "proposition": what happens to a proposition with no support in its batch. "count" (the default) keeps it, as before, and counts it in $extra$propositions_unsupported. "drop" drops it as invented, counts it in $extra$propositions_dropped as well, and warns (gr_proposition_dropped); a batch left with no proposition is kept as written. Untested.

proposition_context_tokens

For method = "proposition": how many tokens from the end of the batch before each batch's request carries, as context the model may use to resolve what the batch refers back to but is told not to decompose. Taken from the document, so the batches still run independently. [0, 2000], default 0, which sends each batch alone, as before. Untested.

packing

How paragraph, sentence, recursive, structural and semantic pack their units into chunks. "greedy" (the default) fills each chunk to max_tokens and leaves the remainder in the last, as before: 1,250 tokens under a 500 cap become 500, 500 and 250. "balanced" keeps the number of chunks greedy packing makes, k, and evens their sizes: it cuts the units at the unit boundaries nearest to each k-th of the total tokens (about 420 each in that example). No unit is split for it: when a unit is longer than max_tokens, or a run between two cuts does not fit under it, the greedy chunks are kept. Untested.

runt_merge

Which way a chunk under min_tokens is merged. "backward" (the default) merges it into the chunk before, as before, so a runt that is the first chunk stays on its own. "both" also merges a first chunk under min_tokens forward into the second, when the two fit under max_tokens. Nothing is merged at min_tokens = 0. Untested.

...

Extra fields for custom segmenters.

Value

A list of class gr_segment_spec.

Out-of-range values

Arguments are clamped into a usable range and the change is warned about, never applied silently: max_tokens [32, 1e6], overlap_tokens [0, max_tokens - 1], min_tokens [0, max_tokens], semantic_window [1, 10], semantic_percentile [50, 99.5], proposition_batch_tokens [200, 4000].

Where the defaults come from

Each setting's default, its tier and the evidence behind the value, as in gr_read_spec(). context_reply_tokens, context_document_tokens and proposition_reply_tokens were constants in the code; they are stored in the spec only when they are not their default, so a default spec keeps the store and cache keys it had before they existed.

  • context_source (default "metadata", advanced): untested. The source that makes no request; not compared with "llm".

  • max_tokens (default 1200, basic): untested. Set when the segmenters were written; not tuned.

  • overlap_tokens (default 0, basic): untested. No overlap, so no text is sent twice; not compared.

  • min_tokens (default 0, advanced): untested. No merging of small chunks; not compared.

  • method (default "paragraph", basic): untested. A segmenter that needs no model or embedder; not compared with the others.

  • separators (default NULL, advanced): untested. Not a tuned value: NULL takes recursive's own cascade.

  • prefix_section (default TRUE, advanced): untested. Set when structural was written; not compared.

  • semantic_window (default 2, advanced): untested. Set when semantic was written; not tuned.

  • semantic_percentile (default 90, advanced): untested. Set when semantic was written; not tuned.

  • proposition_batch_tokens (default 900, advanced): untested. Set when proposition was written; not tuned.

  • parallel (default NULL, advanced): untested. Not a tuned value: NULL follows gr_options("parallel"). It does not change output.

  • context_reply_tokens (default 90, advanced): untested. The cap the code had as a constant; not tuned.

  • context_document_tokens (default 1500, advanced): untested. The length the code had as a constant; not tuned.

  • proposition_reply_tokens (default 2000, advanced): untested. The cap the code had as a constant; not tuned.

  • semantic_threshold (default "percentile", advanced): untested. "percentile" is the rule semantic was written with; not compared with "texttiling".

  • table_packing (default "rows", advanced): untested. "rows" packs a table's rows as any other blocks, as before; not compared with "grouped".

  • proposition_check (default "count", advanced): untested. "count" keeps every proposition, as before, and counts the unsupported; not compared with "drop".

  • proposition_context_tokens (default 0, advanced): untested. 0 sends each batch alone, as before; not tuned.

  • packing (default "greedy", advanced): untested. "greedy" fills each chunk to the cap, as before; not compared with "balanced".

  • runt_merge (default "backward", advanced): untested. "backward" merges into the chunk before, as before; not compared with "both".

See also

gr_segmenters() for the available methods and their costs, gr_segment(), gr_chunk_stats()

Other segmentation functions: gr_check_segmenter(), gr_chunk_stats(), gr_chunks, gr_register_segmenter(), gr_seg_boundaries(), gr_seg_pk(), gr_seg_recall(), gr_segment(), gr_segmenters(), new_chunks()

Examples

gr_segment_spec("semantic", max_tokens = 800, overlap_tokens = 80)$overlap_tokens
#> [1] 80

# An impossible setting is corrected loudly.
suppressWarnings(gr_segment_spec("paragraph", max_tokens = 100,
                                 overlap_tokens = 500)$overlap_tokens)
#> [1] 99
